raw_content: {"answer": "C", "option_text": "Pulmonary sequestration", "reason": "The provided images are axial CT scans (not chest X-rays), showing a retrocardiac cystic lesion with an air-fluid level in the left lower lobe, compensatory hyperinflation/emphysema of the adjacent lung, and a dilated azygos vein. This triad—specifically the systemic arterial supply implied by the vascular finding and the location—is characteristic of intralobar pulmonary sequestration. Pneumonia/abscess typically present acutely without this specific vascular anomaly; bronchogenic cysts are usually fluid-filled without air-fluid levels unless infected but lack the systemic feeder; cancer is less likely given the cystic nature and patient age."}
